About the job

Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

The Kids and Families Compliance team's mission is to build robust infrastructure and essential primitives that enable this organization and other Google services to effectively implement compliance and regulatory requirements for minors. Our team operates with agility across the software stack, responding swiftly to evolving regulations while simultaneously constructing foundational infrastructure.

We are owners and advocates for the underlying design elements, developer platforms, product components, and infrastructure at Google. These are the essential building blocks for excellent, safe, and coherent experiences for our users and drive the pace of innovation for every developer. We look across Google’s products to build central solutions, break down technical barriers and strengthen existing systems. As the Core team, we have a mandate and a unique opportunity to impact important technical decisions across the company.

items.title: New Feature Request: Graduation-year and academic-standing filtering
items.description:
### Improvement

Following up on #2479, could the list support filtering internships by expected graduation year or academic standing? This would help applicants find relevant roles without opening every posting to check the requirements.
I looked through the list-updater code and `listings.json`. The export includes degree types, but not graduation-date windows or freshman/sophomore/junior/senior requirements. The contribution guide mentions that a private service imports listings from Simplify.
Does Simplify already store this information, and could it be included in the automated export? Missing or ambiguous requirements could remain “unknown” rather than implying eligibility.
I’d be interested in contributing filters to the existing search command using that upstream data. Would this be a welcome contribution, and is exposing the necessary data feasible?

items.title: 9 company profiles whose domains no longer exist
items.description:
While checking careers links across `src/companies/` (2026-10-11), I found profiles whose company website and careers page are both unreachable. For these 9, the domain no longer resolves at all (NXDOMAIN, checked twice), so the company looks closed or renamed:

| Profile | Website |
|---|---|
| Cuvette | https://cuvette.tech |
| GitPrime | https://gitprime.com/ (acquired by Pluralsight in 2019) |
| Grou.ps | https://build.gr.ps |
| Impira | https://www.impira.com/ |
| Mobile Jazz | https://mobilejazz.com |
| Park Assist | https://tech.parkassist.com |
| Pathable | https://pathable.com/ |
| Socket Supply Co | https://socketsupply.co |
| Telestax Inc. | https://telestax.com/ |

Related:
- **Interactive Intelligence**: `inin.com` now redirects to Genesys, which acquired it.
- **Bugfender**: its `careers_url` is `https://mobilejazz.com/jobs`, on the dead Mobile Jazz domain above.

CONTRIBUTING says profiles are normally removed when a company no longer meets the criteria, so I didn't want to delete these without asking. Happy to open a PR removing them (and fixing Bugfender's link) if you agree.

(Separately, #2270 updates 9 careers links that moved.)
